newsitem.title: JAPAN: Most Japanese feel Asia hates Japan -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Japanese feel Asia hates Japan -- poll.

text.p: A growing majority of Japanese feel the rest of Asia hates them, a newspaper survey published on Saturday said.
The Asahi Shimbun survey of 3,000 adults on Asian issues also found a majority of Japanese oppose allowing more immigrant workers or refugees into the country from the region.
The "hate" rate was five percentage points up from a similar Asahi Shimbun survey conducted in 1994, the daily said.
Among various age groups, 70 percent of those in their 20s said the felt they were hated by other Asians.

"We might be able to say that the youth, who have the most exchanges with Asia, feel the most pain on the part of Asians," wrote Hisao Mitsuro of the Asahi editorial staff that conducted the survey in September.

The survey said 65 percent of respondents supported maintaining the current level of refugees and immigrant workers from rest of Asia. Japan has a stringent policy on immigrant workers and an even stricter restriction on refugees.

Asked how they viewed Japan's economic relations with the rest of Asia, 47 percent said the Asian economy would grow but that Japan's economy would stagnate, followed by 33 percent who said the economies of both Japan and rest of Asia would grow.

Asked what Japan's main effort should be in ties with Asia, 23 percent said strengthening economic relations, followed by 19 percent for environment issues and 14 percent each for exchanges among citizens and constructing a regional security arrangement.

Forty-seven percent of respondents felt China would be the most influential country in Asia in the next century, followed by the United States with 23 percent, Japan 13 percent and ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, at six percent.
